neighbours.label: a word stating which of two linked things comes first or is the cause ('precedes', 'rather than a cause', 'is absorbed in', 'results in a net reduction')
fire: Researchers now think that poor sleep precedes the build-up of plaque in the brain.
The weight loss is probably a result of the illness rather than a cause of it.
In this merger the smaller firm is absorbed into the larger one.
The extra resistance ultimately results in a net reduction of current.
In most patients the fever comes before the rash appears.
The drop in prices was caused by the surplus, not the other way around.
Low vitamin levels seem to follow the disease rather than trigger it.
The heavy rain led directly to the flooding of the lower town.
quiet: Researchers now measure both sleep quality and plaque levels in the brain.
The weight loss was recorded at every visit during the illness.
In this merger both firms kept their offices and their names.
The extra resistance was measured with a simple meter in the lab.
In most patients both the fever and the rash were mild.
The prices and the surplus were both reported in the same table.
Vitamin levels were checked in every patient with the disease.
The heavy rain and the flooding were in all the local papers.

notes: Card: preced(es), rather (than a cause), absorbed, reduction; the - pole fires on alternatives and questions (or, whether, 'is it the other way around'), the open side of the same causal-order question.
